req.title: Password hashing uses generate_password_hash
req.statement: The system shall store passwords via werkzeug generate_password_hash rather than plaintext.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-035 requires that passwords are stored via werkzeug's generate_password_hash rather than plaintext. Tests must verify: (1) positive - registration succeeds and the stored password is a hash (not plaintext), (2) negative - plaintext password is NOT stored in the database, (3) boundary - the hash can be verified with check_password_hash (round-trip), and (4) additional coverage for state transition (register then login succeeds, proving hash is valid). We directly inspect the database row after registration to assert the stored value is a werkzeug hash string, not the original plaintext. We also verify login works (check_password_hash succeeds), and that the stored value differs from the plaintext input.

tests.name: test_password_stored_as_hash_not_plaintext
actions: Query the database for the stored password of 'TestHashUser'
expected: Stored password is NOT equal to 'myplainpass'
Stored password starts with 'scrypt:' or 'pbkdf2:' (werkzeug hash prefix)
Stored password length is greater than len('myplainpass')
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
plain = 'myplainpass'
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'TestHashUser', 'password': plain})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = ?", ('TestHashUser',)).fetchone()
    stored = row['password']

assert stored != plain, 'Password must not be stored as plaintext'
assert len(stored) > len(plain), 'Hash must be longer than plaintext'
assert (stored.startswith('scrypt:') or stored.startswith('pbkdf2:')), f'Expected werkzeug hash prefix, got: {stored[:20]}'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_hash_round_trip_check_password_hash
actions: Call werkzeug check_password_hash(stored, 'stone') -> must be True
Call werkzeug check_password_hash(stored, 'STONE') -> must be False (case-sensitive)
Call werkzeug check_password_hash(stored, '') -> must be False
trace: R-FLASKR-035: hash produced by generate_password_hash must be verifiable by check_password_hash
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
plain = 'stone'
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'BVAUser', 'password': plain})
assert r.status_code == 302

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = ?", ('BVAUser',)).fetchone()
    stored = row['password']

assert check_password_hash(stored, plain) == True, 'Correct password must verify'
assert check_password_hash(stored, 'STONE') == False, 'Wrong case must not verify'
assert check_password_hash(stored, '') == False, 'Empty password must not verify'
assert check_password_hash(stored, plain + ' ') == False, 'Padded password must not verify'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_login_succeeds_after_hashed_registration
actions: Assert login redirects to index (hash was stored correctly and is verifiable)
trace: R-FLASKR-035: hash stored by generate_password_hash must allow successful login via check_password_hash
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r_reg = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'STCUser', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r_reg.status_code == 302
assert r_reg.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'STCUser', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302
assert r_login.headers['Location'] == '/'

r_wrong = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'STCUser', 'password': 'wrongpass'})
assert r_wrong.status_code == 200
assert b'Incorrect password.' in r_wrong.data
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_different_passwords_produce_different_hashes
preconditions: Two users registered with different passwords
actions: Assert the two hashes are different from each other and from their plaintexts
expected: hash_A != hash_B (different inputs produce different outputs)
trace: R-FLASKR-035: generate_password_hash must produce distinct hashes for distinct passwords
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'UserA', 'password': 'stone'})
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'UserB', 'password': 'cloud'})

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row_a = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = ?", ('UserA',)).fetchone()
    row_b = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = ?", ('UserB',)).fetchone()
    hash_a = row_a['password']
    hash_b = row_b['password']

assert hash_a != 'stone', 'UserA password must not be plaintext'
assert hash_b != 'cloud', 'UserB password must not be plaintext'
assert hash_a != hash_b, 'Different passwords must produce different hashes'
assert len(hash_a) > 10, 'Hash must be non-trivially long'
assert len(hash_b) > 10, 'Hash must be non-trivially long'
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_same_password_produces_salted_different_hashes
preconditions: Two users registered with the SAME password
actions: Assert the two hashes differ (salting ensures uniqueness)
expected: hash_1 != hash_2 (salted hashes differ even for same plaintext)
trace: R-FLASKR-035: generate_password_hash uses salt so identical passwords yield distinct stored values
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db
from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'SaltUser1', 'password': 'stone'})
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'SaltUser2', 'password': 'stone'})

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    h1 = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = ?", ('SaltUser1',)).fetchone()['password']
    h2 = db.execute("SELECT password FROM user WHERE username = ?", ('SaltUser2',)).fetchone()['password']

assert h1 != 'stone'
assert h2 != 'stone'
assert h1 != h2, 'Salted hashes for same password must differ'
assert check_password_hash(h1, 'stone') == True
assert check_password_hash(h2, 'stone') == True
os.unlink(path)
